children: Kinetik’s third-quarter revenue and net income attributable to Class A shareholders rose year over year. Higher NGL and condensate sales volumes and commodity prices drove revenue growth; lower operating and general and administrative expenses also supported results, partly offset by higher cost of sales and weaker equity earnings from unconsolidated affiliates.
¹ Reported as “Total operating revenues”. ² Reported as “Net income attributable to holders of Class A Common Stock”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: Segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to $203.6M, driven primarily by higher operating revenues, partly offset by increased cost of sales.
: Segment Adjusted EBITDA fell 18% to $78.5M, mainly reflecting lower proportionate EMI EBITDA following the EPIC equity-interest divestiture.
: NGL and condensate volumes sold increased 32%; their prices rose 32% and 35%, respectively, year over year.
: Construction was completed and the pipeline entered service in June 2026, providing approximately 150 MMcf/d of initial rich gas throughput capacity.
